questions.q: What is the paper's core novelty relative to earlier end-to-end audiovisual speech recognizers?
questions.answer: It claims the first end-to-end audiovisual word recognizer on a large in-the-wild dataset that learns from raw mouth-region pixels and raw waveforms, using residual-network front ends and BGRU stream/fusion layers. The authors contrast this with earlier systems that used MFCCs or spectrograms and cite their training procedure and modality-specific recurrent modelling as further distinctions.

questions.q: How much does audiovisual fusion improve recognition in clean audio and under babble noise?
questions.answer: The reported clean comparison is a 0.3% absolute increase over both audio-only systems. Under babble noise, audiovisual classification exceeds end-to-end audio by 1.3%, 3.9%, and 14.1% at 5, 0, and -5 dB SNR; end-to-end audio exceeds MFCC by 0.9%, 3.5%, and 7.5% at those same SNRs. The paper does not give uncertainty estimates or explicitly map these result tables/plots to a split.

questions.q: Which benchmark conditions and reproducibility details should the review qualify?
questions.answer: The paper describes LRW's 500-word task and train/validation/test counts, but does not explicitly identify the split used for every headline result, state speaker/session disjointness, report seeds or repeated-run variation, fully specify the noisy-test mixture, give all normalization statistics, report a chance baseline, or provide significance testing.

questions.q: What limitations or scope boundaries do the authors acknowledge?
questions.answer: Visual input contributes only marginally in clean audio; end-to-end audio training is more effortful than the MFCC baseline; the present output is an isolated-word label rather than sentence recognition; and adaptive modality weighting is left for future work. The cited visual comparison using tracked landmarks also has a different ROI from the proposed system.

questions.q: Writer: is the MFCC baseline given the same convolutional front end and augmentation as the end-to-end audio stream?
questions.answer: Sec. 5: it is a 2-layer BGRU on 13 MFCCs plus deltas, trained the same way as the BGRU networks of Sec. 4.3 but longer with early stopping; no convolutional front end is described (writer grep of the passage).
